Question B-001-020-003.

Why the correct answer is right: International amateur communication is allowed when administrations have kept the communication path open. The permission depends on administrations as well as the wishes of the two operators.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Certification requirements in the amateur radio service are prescribed in the Radio Regulations": The international-communication rule is about communications and objections; certification details are handled by administrations.
- sourceIndex 2: "Radiocommunications between certified amateur radio operators are always permitted even if a country objects": An administration's objection matters, so certified operators cannot override it by mutual agreement.
- sourceIndex 3: "Amateur radio operators may recover reasonable costs from transmitting third-party messages": Cost recovery would make amateur traffic resemble a paid message service, and it is not the ITU provision on international communications.
